> **Narrowed again 2026-10-17 (backlog sweep, second pass).**
>
> **Resolved so far:** PR #1030 (`fix/778-test-isolation`, `34487e7ca`).
> - Item 1: the gh866 poison test and `test_gh809...::test_a_destamped_parquet_rebuilds_once_and_does_not_loop` run in a private `LSMS_DATA_DIR` (copied country subtree, `dvc-cache` symlinked). Two raw readers of Nigeria `crop_production` during the gh866 cell: wrong reads 30/1,065 -> 0/615, `FileNotFoundError` 615 -> 0; shared md5 unchanged.
> - Item 2: `TestBuiltTable` and the `exists()`-then-read siblings (`test_id_format_id_canonical`, `test_food_prices_dtype`, `test_sample`) make the read the check.
> - Item 3 measured: cold concurrent GhanaLSS `food_acquired` builders (simultaneous, and staggered at 4 of 7 waves) are byte-identical on disk to a serial cold build (5,340,606 rows, 7-wave manifest, same md5); 1,394 metadata polls never saw a partial aggregate. **Does not reproduce; no library change.**
>
> **Remaining (this issue):**
> 1. **(Tests.) Other tests still rebuild in the SHARED root under `LSMS_NO_CACHE`:** gh866's `test_a_wave_produced_table_is_never_evicted` (Togo `plot_features`), `test_ghanalss_interview_date.py`, `test_ghanalss_visit_derivations.py`, `test_guyana_index_uniqueness.py`, `test_gh323_site4_dfs_merge.py`, `test_india_employment_activity_index.py`. They write correct data, but for a country-only table the #866 eviction deletes `var/` before the rebuild, opening the same `FileNotFoundError` window for concurrent readers. Not measured. Next step: check which of their cells delete `var/` at all, then give those the same private-root fixture.
> 2. **(Library.) `assume_cache_fresh` has the same `exists()`-then-read race** (`country.py` ~:4158-4182: `exists()`, then `read_parquet_cache_waves`, then `get_dataframe`). Fix direction: try the read and fall through to the ordinary path on `FileNotFoundError`.
> 3. **(Note, carried.)** `assume_cache_fresh` serves a country script's unstamped output while it sits at the final path. Identical for Nigeria `crop_production`; untested elsewhere.
>
> Not a residual, noted so nobody chases it: #891's manifest records requested rather than producing waves, but no partial build occurred in either concurrent trial.

<details><summary>Previous issue text (narrowed 2026-10-17 morning, with the original report)</summary>

> **Narrowed again 2026-10-17 (Sue).** This follows the 2026-10-17 `cache-verify` element (diagnosis only, no code change).
>
> **Resolved so far:**
> - The original GhanaLSS `nan == 5570` failure was #808, a retired country script that renamed household 101332 to `101332_0`.
> - It no longer reproduces. A cold `cache clear --country GhanaLSS` build followed by the GhanaLSS test gives `10 passed`.
> - Step (1) landed via #891.
>
> **What the 2026-10-17 Nigeria `TestBuiltTable` flake actually was:** not a partial aggregate and not a torn write.
> - `test_gh866_stale_country_parquet_not_laundered.py::test_a_poisoned_country_parquet_is_REBUILT_not_served` deliberately writes a 5-row slice into the SHARED `var/<table>.parquet` for 9 cells, and keeps the wave manifest.
> - Readers in other xdist workers that read raw or use `assume_cache_fresh=True` get that frame. Nigeria `crop_production` with two processes: raw reads 12/315 wrong, trusting API 2/31 wrong, ordinary API 0/24.
> - A writer lock would not help: the poison is a complete atomic write, and those readers never check a hash.
>
> **Remaining (this issue):**
> 1. **(Test-only.) Isolate the mutating tests.** Run the gh866 poison test, and `test_gh809_hashless_country_parquet.py::test_a_destamped_parquet_rebuilds_once_and_does_not_loop`, in a private `LSMS_DATA_DIR`: copy the country's cache subtree into `tmp_path` and symlink `dvc-cache`.
> 2. **(Test-only.) Close the `exists()`-then-read race in `TestBuiltTable`.** Since #866 a rebuild deletes the file first; 999 of 1,591 raw reads during six rebuilds hit `FileNotFoundError`. Make the read itself the check (`except FileNotFoundError: skip`).
> 3. **(Measurement.) Cold concurrent builders are still unmeasured.** Run two cold GhanaLSS `food_acquired` builders in one private root and diff against a serial build. #891's manifest records the waves a build was asked for, not those that produced rows, so a partial build would still claim full coverage. Act only if it reproduces.
> 4. **(Note.)** `assume_cache_fresh` serves a country script's unstamped output while it sits at the final path. It is identical for Nigeria `crop_production`; untested elsewhere.

*Original text, kept for the evidence:*

pytest -n against a cold shared cache: a country aggregate built from a partial wave set caches as fresh, so data tests flake indistinguishably from regressions

## What happened

A full-suite run (`pytest --no-purge -n 32`) on a **cold** GhanaLSS cache failed a data-correctness test:

```
FAILED tests/test_panel_id_collisions.py::test_ghanalss_split_household_food_not_summed_into_one
E   AssertionError: household 101332's 1988-89 food expenditure is the sum of two different households (GH #548)
E   assert nan == 5570.0 ± 0.00557
```

The data is correct. `GhanaLSS/var/food_acquired.parquet` has household `101332` with 22 rows summing to exactly `5570.0`, `101332_1` exists separately, and the test passes on a serial re-run (`20 passed`). It is a **flake that is indistinguishable from a data regression** — it cost a full investigation to rule out a real defect after 12 PRs had just merged.

## Why — and it is not a torn write

`local_tools.to_parquet` is already atomic (PID-temp file + `os.replace`, documented as being for exactly this), so no reader ever sees a truncated file. The mtimes tell the actual story:

| file | written |
|---|---|
| `GhanaLSS/1987-88/_/food_acquired.parquet` | 07:59 |
| `GhanaLSS/1988-89/_/food_acquired.parquet` | 07:59 |
| `…1991-92 / 1998-99 / 2005-06` | 08:00 |
| `…2012-13` | 08:01 |
| `…2016-17` | 08:02 |
| **`GhanaLSS/var/food_acquired.parquet`** | **08:02** |
| pytest run ends | 08:02:48 |

With 32 xdist workers and a cold cache, several workers begin building the same country table at once. One completes a **country-level aggregate from the set of wave parquets that existed at that moment**, writes it atomically, and it is then a *complete-looking* file carrying a *valid content hash* — so every later reader trusts it. A worker reading in that window gets a frame that is silently missing waves (or households), and `.xs(...)` raises `KeyError`.

This is a **concurrency instance of #675** ("a degraded build caches as fresh"): same failure shape, different cause — there a dropped sub-df, here a partial wave set.

## Why not "just warm the cache first"

Populating the whole corpus is expensive in both compute and disk, and it makes a parallel test run depend on a preceding serial build of everything it might touch. The suite should be honest on a cold cache instead.

## Suggested direction

1. **Record what an aggregate was built from.** When a country-level table is concatenated from waves, stamp the contributing wave set into the parquet's schema metadata (beside `lsms_cache_hash` / `lsms_grain_audit`). A reader can then tell "built from 2 of 7 waves" from "this country has 2 waves", which is exactly the distinction nothing can currently make.
2. **Treat an incomplete aggregate as not-fresh**, so it is rebuilt rather than trusted — the cache-freshness gate already has the hook.
3. **Let data-gated tests skip rather than fail** when the stamp shows an in-progress/partial build: `pytest.skip("cache incomplete — concurrent build in progress")`. A flaky *failure* on shared state is worse than a skip, because it trains readers to discount real failures.

(1) is what makes (3) possible; without it a test cannot distinguish the two cases, which is the root of the problem.

## Related

- #675 — a degraded build caches as fresh (same shape, different cause)
- #719 — `conftest.py` purging Uganda's parquets against the **shared** cache; same underlying assumption that the suite controls a cache it does not

Found while verifying the merged tree after 12 PRs; the 2 remaining failures in that run were the pre-existing #772.

— Sue

</details>
title: Tests that rebuild in the SHARED root under LSMS_NO_CACHE still open the #866 delete-then-rebuild window; assume_cache_fresh has an exists()-then-read race
